title: The Second Bakery
premise: Ivo Almeida, a ghostwriter hired to pen the memoirs of celebrity baker Marisa Duarte, discovers the rival bakery empire was built on a stolen recipe — one that belongs to his own estranged family. When he needs a date for the Almeida family reunion, he recruits Marisa's estranged sister Beatriz, a pastry chef who walked away from the business years ago, and their fake romance turns real over shared dough and old grievances. As Ivo's manuscript deadline collides with the town's centennial bread festival, loyalty to his client, truth for his family, and love for Beatriz pull him in three directions, and publishing the memoir as written would destroy everyone he cares about. In the end, Ivo burns the false chapters, Beatriz bakes her grandmother's recipe at the festival under her own name, and they choose each other after the last train home has already gone.
about_author: Yara Kavanagh is a former line cook who traded kitchen shifts for manuscript pages and now writes love stories set wherever flour meets feeling. She lives in a coastal town famous for exactly one bakery, which she refuses to name out of loyalty to all of them.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Proofing Room
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Hired to ghostwrite Marisa Duarte's triumphant memoir, Ivo interviews her in her flagship bakery and notices she flinches whenever her sister's name surfaces. He takes the job for the money and the distance from his own failed novel. Emotional beat: wary ambition shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A letter summons Ivo to the Almeida family reunion, where his grandmother will announce the fate of the family's shuttered bakery building. Dreading arriving alone and interrogated, he impulsively asks Beatriz Duarte — the woman he's seen arguing with Marisa through a window — to pose as his girlfriend. Emotional beat: desperation dressed up as charm.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz agrees to the fake date because it gets her into the reunion where her late mother's recipe box is stored — and away from Marisa's orbit. They negotiate rules: no real feelings, no questions about the past. Both break a rule within an hour. Emotional beat: prickly chemistry.

chapters.title: Reunion, First Course
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The reunion opens with casseroles and ambushes; Ivo's aunt quizzes Beatriz about their relationship while Beatriz quietly locates the recipe box, locked in a display cabinet. Ivo watches her lie beautifully and feels something tilt. Emotional beat: performance becoming perilously easy.

chapters.title: Dessert Was a Mistake
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Asked to bring dessert, Beatriz improvises her mother's honey cake; Ivo tastes it and goes still — it's the flavor of his childhood, the recipe his family claims was stolen decades ago. By candlelight, the fake kiss they stage for the relatives lingers too long. Emotional beat: sweetness curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: What Marisa Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Back at work, Ivo presses Marisa on the founding story; her polished legend of 'inventing' the signature loaf cracks at the edges. She gifts him a generous bonus and a warning about digging. He transcribes her version anyway, hating how good it sounds. Emotional beat: complicity tightening.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz finally opens the recipe box and finds her mother's handwriting beside a newspaper clipping from thirty years ago: two sisters, one bakery, one betrayal. She realizes Ivo is the grandson of the wronged sister. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Confrontation Over Cold Coffee
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Beatriz confronts Ivo: you're writing the lie that buried my mother. Ivo defends himself badly, then admits what he's suspected since the honey cake. They agree to an uneasy alliance — find the proof before the memoir ships. Emotional beat: enemies becoming co-conspirators.

chapters.title: Archives and Alibis
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Research montage: county records, a retired food columnist, a microfilm photo showing both grandmothers in one kitchen. Meanwhile Marisa grows suspicious of Ivo's questions and moves the manuscript deadline up. Emotional beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Practice Run
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. To test whether the old recipe can be revived, Beatriz and Ivo bake together in her tiny apartment kitchen at midnight — flour everywhere, laughter inevitable, a near-kiss interrupted by a timer. It's the first time either has baked with someone instead of against them. Emotional beat: tenderness breaking through.

chapters.title: Marisa Makes Her Move
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marisa offers Ivo a partnership stake if he delivers the memoir early and 'keeps the family stuff vague.' The money would clear his debts; the silence would bury the truth. He says yes and immediately hates himself. Emotional beat: corruption knocking politely.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. The centennial bread festival announces its centerpiece bake-off; entry requires a family recipe with provenance. Beatriz enters under the Almeida-Duarte joint name, forcing the townsfolk — and Marisa — to reckon with the shared history. Emotional beat: quiet defiance going public.

chapters.title: Deadline Pressure
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo drafts the sanitized memoir, each false chapter costing him more sleep. He hides the archive evidence in a safety-deposit box and tells no one, including Beatriz, ashamed of the deal he struck. Emotional beat: guilt metastasizing.

chapters.title: Caught Between Courses
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz discovers Ivo signed Marisa's deal when a courier delivers a contract copy to the wrong address. Feeling betrayed twice over — by Marisa then by Ivo — she withdraws from the festival and stops answering his calls. Emotional beat: heartbreak with receipts.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Testimony
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo visits his grandmother, who reveals she never wanted the feud — she wanted her sister back, and the recipe was never the point. She gives him the original handwritten card and her blessing to tell the truth however it costs. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: Burning the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On delivery day, Ivo submits a different document: a resignation letter and the evidence file, publicly withdrawing his name from the memoir. Marisa threatens litigation; he walks out past the ovens he once admired. Emotional beat: costly integrity, finally chosen.

chapters.title: Last Train Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Humiliated and exposed, Beatriz decides to leave town the night before the festival. Ivo races to the station, lays the original recipe card on the platform between them, and asks nothing except that she stay. The last train departs without her. Emotional beat: the grand gesture done small and true.

chapters.title: Festival Morning
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Beatriz bakes the honey loaf at dawn in the festival tent, hands shaking, using both families' names on the entry card. Marisa arrives unannounced, watches the crowd gather, and says nothing — yet. Emotional beat: vulnerability performed in public.

chapters.title: The Bake-Off Verdict
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The judges award Beatriz first prize for provenance and flavor; the crowd learns the true history as she tells it plainly, without venom. Marisa approaches the table, and the sisters face each other across one cooling loaf. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by unfinished business.

chapters.title: Sisters, One Kitchen
chapters.summary: Beatriz's POV. Marisa privately admits the theft, then asks not for forgiveness but to bake alongside her sister once. They knead side by side in the festival kitchen while Ivo keeps watch outside, letting them have it. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. With the festival ending and trains gone, Ivo and Beatriz walk the empty platform and admit the fake date ended somewhere around dessert months ago. No grand declarations — just a plan to open a small second bakery together, named for both grandmothers. Emotional beat: love chosen without spectacle.

chapters.title: Opening Day
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. The Second Bakery opens its doors: the true memoir published independently, the sisters supplying bread, the grandmother cutting the ribbon. Ivo begins writing his own novel at a corner table while Beatriz calls out the first order. Emotional beat: second chances, kept warm.
